correctness.rationale: The constant-annihilation property gives a well-defined Gini quotient. The interval-crossing identity expresses each output pair difference as n^{-1} times a complete bipartite sum over a contiguous interval. Counting its separating intervals gives N_{p,q}=(q-p)(n-q+p), and the upper bound. The e1 ramp has ratio (n+1)/6, proving failure for all n>=6. A layer-cake/coarea representation reduces the small-order sharp coefficient to all binary cuts. The exact checker exhausts every nontrivial cut in dimensions 2..5, yielding 1/2,2/3,5/6,1. No all-order exact norm is claimed.

value.rationale: Identifies the exact first dimension at which a natural mean-centered discrete antiderivative ceases to be nonexpansive under a complete-pair dispersion seminorm. Also proves linear dimension growth between two explicit universal bounds and exhibits the ramp witness for every higher order. The sharp cutoff is a motivated stability invariant, not an arbitrary finite slice, and does not rely on speculative downstream applications.
